{{Quote|What has happened to our home? What has happened to Castle Renais? How did it come to be so ruined? So desolated?|[[Ephraim]]}}

'''Ruled by Madness''' (Japanese: {{hl|荒れ果てた王都|Arehateta ōto}} ''Desolated capital'') is the sixteenth chapter of {{FE8}}.

==Plot==
{{main|Ruled by Madness/Script (Eirika)|Ruled by Madness/Script (Ephraim)}}

[[Eirika]], [[Ephraim]], and company approach Castle [[Renais]]. Ephraim wonders how Renais has become so desolate; [[Seth]] relays spies' reports, that [[Orson]] has been put in charge of Renais but neglects it. Ephraim and Eirika resolve to liberate their home from Orson's misrule. [[Myrrh]] requests that she be allowed to aid the twins with her [[dragonstone]]; Ephraim agrees, on the condition that she not stray far from them.

In Castle Renais, Orson enters his chamber and speaks to [[Monica (The Sacred Stones)|Monica]]; [[Lyon]] and [[Riev]] later enter as well. In Eirika's route, Riev speaks to Orson, informing him that Eirika and Ephraim are coming for him and pose a threat to Monica; as Riev and Lyon leave, Lyon experiences a bout of pain, but Riev assures him it will soon pass, and the two teleport away. In Ephraim's route, Lyon informs Orson of Ephraim's approach instead, reminding Orson that he is the one who resurrected Monica. In both routes, Orson leaves Monica to deal with the twins, promising Monica he will return.

Orson is eventually defeated in battle, and the castle is secured. Seth leads Ephraim and Eirika to Orson's room, where they find the corpse of Monica, reanimated by similar magic as [[Vigarde]]; Ephraim elects to destroy Monica's corpse. At the throne, Ephraim resolves to rebuild Renais when he becomes king, but doubts he will be accepted. Seth then takes Ephraim and Eirika outside, where crowds cheer; Seth informs them the crowd cheers for the end of Orson's rule, not the start of Ephraim's, and Ephraim decides to dedicate his rule to their happiness.

Ephraim, Eirika, and Seth then return to the throne to find Renais's [[Sacred Stone (object)|Sacred Stone]]. Eirika and Ephraim raise their bracelets, which begin to shine as the throne moves to reveal a stairway; down the stairs, they find the Sacred Stone of Renais, and their bracelets react to the power of the stone, allowing the twins to [[class change]]. Seth then retrieves Renais's [[Sacred Twin]]s, giving Ephraim [[Siegmund]] and Eirika [[Sieglinde]]. The twins return to the throne room with the Sacred Stone; [[L'Arachel]] suggests they travel to [[Rausten]], which houses the last remaining stone, and the group agrees to travel with L'Arachel as their guide.

==Strategy==
{{strategy}}
The main time pressure on this map is the thieves that spawn as reinforcements. The conditions and turn for their spawning varies by the route. For Ephraim's route, the turn 17 thief is far too late to pose a threat to the treasure at any reasonable pace of play, and the turn 6 thief can be defeated without ever having stepping foot in the castle. Once again stats staffs are present so don’t forget to take [[Restore]]s. On Ephraim's route the main one of consequence is the Berserk staff near the back entrance, which can easily be eliminated with a javelin before it gets a second shot off. Others are often more annoying than deadly, but should still be prepared for. 

While Ephraim starts further back, closer to the rear entrance, this doesn't necessarily mean you should use it. The narrow pass and forest make it cumbersome to use, and it doesn't really bypass any real threats. At most only a small force is needed to remove the Berserk bishop, and help stop the turn 6 thief, and this team doesn’t even need to ''enter'' the castle for these. The forest leading up to the back door is however a fine place to station a unit for dealing with the reinforcements that spawn after entering the castle.

Ephraim’s version of the map has several siege tome users where Eirika has only a single Purge user with restrictive AI. The Eclipse tome Druids are no serious threat and can largely be ignored: They can’t kill, have minimal accuracy, and only reinforcements move after them so they likely won’t set up a kill even if they do hit. The Purge Sage is a more serious threat, but his spawning is based on condition, not turn, so it’s easy to avoid him till you’re ready if you know the trigger.

In versions of the map where Orson has a Runesword, he is easily dealt with by placing a magic user at 2 range, as he lacks the power to apply damage to high resistance units and the resistance to take their hits. Otherwise deal with him like any other boss.

==Trivia==
*In the Japanese version, Orson carries a Silver Lance and a Runesword on Eirika's route, and a Silver Sword and a Spear on Ephraim's route. This was swapped in the Western version. Also in the Japanese version, Orson wields the Silver Sword or Silver Lance by default rather than the Spear or Runesword.
